title: Seb Coe: Athlete of the Year Voting Under Review
excerpt: Seb Coe said World Athletics is reviewing how World Athlete of the Year is voted. Why to judge your own progress on measurable results instead.
body:
World Athletics president Seb Coe said during an end-of-year media call on December 16, 2025, that the World Athlete of the Year voting process is under review. Under the current format, votes from the World Athletics Council count for 50%, the World Athletics Family for 25% and a public social-media vote for 25%, and vote totals are not published. The 2025 awards drew criticism, including from Noah Lyles.

Awards and rankings decided by votes will always be more subjective than race results. For everyday runners, the useful lesson is to judge your own progress by things you can measure: times, consistency and how you race, rather than by outside recognition.

Set your own benchmarks, such as a target time, a weekly mileage or a number of training weeks completed, and track them honestly. Measurable progress is a more reliable source of motivation than anyone else's verdict.

Sources: LetsRun.com; SportBible
keyTakeaway: Judge your progress on what you can measure and control, not on rankings or awards.
